quests.sentence: Hi team, I've attached the revised budget for your review.
quests.hint: The attaching is already done and directly relevant to this message right now.
quests.explanation: Have attached is the present perfect form, connecting a completed action to its relevance in the current email.

quests.sentence: I'll finalize the numbers once I hear back from finance.
quests.hint: This depends on something that hasn't happened yet.
quests.explanation: Will finalize is the simple future form, describing a planned action waiting on a future condition.

quests.sentence: We're finalizing the Q3 numbers this week.
quests.hint: 'This week' points to a task currently underway, not a finished habit.
quests.explanation: Are finalizing is the present progressive form, describing an action in progress during the current week.

quests.sentence: The migration has been running since midnight without any errors.
quests.hint: This emphasizes the continuing process, still going since it started.
quests.explanation: Has been running is the present perfect progressive form, emphasizing an ongoing process continuing from a past starting point.

quests.sentence: We completed the first phase of the migration on schedule.
quests.hint: This describes one finished stage as a completed event.
quests.explanation: Completed is the simple past form, describing a finished stage of the project.

quests.sentence: By Friday, we'll have migrated the entire database.
quests.hint: Friday is the point by which this whole task will be finished.
quests.explanation: Will have migrated is the future perfect form, describing a task expected to be complete by a future point.

quests.sentence: Thank you for taking the time to meet with me yesterday.
quests.hint: 'Yesterday' names a specific, finished day.
quests.explanation: The reference to yesterday's meeting takes the simple past, describing a completed event.

quests.sentence: I really enjoyed learning more about the team's current projects.
quests.hint: This describes a specific, finished experience from that meeting.
quests.explanation: Enjoyed is the simple past form, describing a completed reaction to a specific past event.

quests.sentence: I look forward to hearing from you about next steps.
quests.hint: This is a standard, polite closing expression describing the writer's present attitude.
quests.explanation: Look forward is the simple present form, used in this fixed, polite expression about an ongoing attitude.

quests.sentence: As you can see from this slide, revenue has increased steadily over the past year.
quests.hint: This describes a trend over a period leading up to now, still relevant to the presentation.
quests.explanation: Has increased is the present perfect form, describing a change over time that remains relevant to the present.

quests.sentence: Before I go further, let me recap what we covered earlier in the presentation.
quests.hint: This refers to specific material already presented earlier in the same talk.
quests.explanation: Covered is the simple past form, describing content already presented at an earlier, specific point.

quests.sentence: By the end of this talk, you'll understand exactly how the new system works.
quests.hint: This is a promise about what the audience will know afterward.
quests.explanation: Will understand is the simple future form, describing an expected future outcome for the audience.

quests.sentence: I haven't submitted my assignment yet because I'm still waiting on feedback from my group.
quests.hint: Focus on the first half — this task remains incomplete up to now.
quests.explanation: Haven't submitted is the negative present perfect form, describing a task still incomplete as of now.

quests.sentence: Professor Diaz posted the updated syllabus last night.
quests.hint: 'Last night' names a specific, finished time.
quests.explanation: Posted is the simple past form, describing a completed action at a specific past time.

quests.sentence: Starting next semester, the department will require an extra lab session.
quests.hint: This is a planned change for a semester that hasn't started yet.
quests.explanation: Will require is the simple future form, describing a planned future requirement.

quests.sentence: Our flight got delayed, so we're stuck at the gate for another two hours.
quests.hint: Focus on the delay itself — a completed event that caused the current situation.
quests.explanation: Got delayed is the simple past form, describing the completed event that led to the current wait.

quests.sentence: We've never had this much trouble with a connecting flight before.
quests.hint: This is about experience up to now, not one specific occasion.
quests.explanation: Have had is the present perfect form, describing an experience, or lack of one, up to the present.

quests.sentence: By the time we land, we'll have been traveling for almost eighteen hours straight.
quests.hint: This measures a long stretch of ongoing travel leading up to a future point.
quests.explanation: Will have been traveling is the future perfect progressive form, emphasizing duration continuing up to a future point.

quests.sentence: I've been having headaches on and off for the past two weeks.
quests.hint: This emphasizes a recurring, ongoing pattern over the last two weeks.
quests.explanation: Have been having is the present perfect progressive form, emphasizing a continuing pattern over a recent period.

quests.sentence: The doctor recommended I cut back on caffeine.
quests.hint: This describes a specific piece of advice given at a past appointment.
quests.explanation: Recommended is the simple past form, describing a completed action from a specific past visit.

quests.sentence: I'll schedule a follow-up appointment once the test results come back.
quests.hint: This plan depends on something that hasn't happened yet.
quests.explanation: Will schedule is the simple future form, describing a plan that depends on a future condition; notice that 'come back', inside the once-clause, stays in the simple present even though it refers to the future.

quests.sentence: Your payment has been processed and should reflect in your account within two business days.
quests.hint: This focuses on a completed action that's directly relevant right now.
quests.explanation: Has been processed is the present perfect passive form, connecting a completed action to its current relevance.

quests.sentence: The bank charged an overdraft fee last week that I wasn't expecting.
quests.hint: 'Last week' names a specific, finished time.
quests.explanation: Charged is the simple past form, describing a completed event at a specific past time.

quests.sentence: By next month, I'll have paid off the entire balance.
quests.hint: Next month is the point by which this goal will be reached.
quests.explanation: Will have paid off is the future perfect form, describing a goal expected to be complete by a future point.

quests.sentence: I'm still experiencing the same error even after restarting my device twice.
quests.hint: The problem is continuing right now, despite the attempted fix.
quests.explanation: Am experiencing is the present progressive form, describing a problem that is still ongoing.

quests.sentence: Our engineers identified the root cause this morning.
quests.hint: This morning is treated here as a finished part of the day with a completed result.
quests.explanation: Identified is the simple past form, describing a completed discovery at a specific past time.

quests.sentence: The fix will roll out to all users by tomorrow afternoon.
quests.hint: This is a planned release for a time that hasn't arrived yet.
quests.explanation: Will roll out is the simple future form, describing a planned future release.

quests.sentence: Can't talk right now — I'm driving and traffic's insane.
quests.hint: This is happening at this very moment, which is why a call isn't possible.
quests.explanation: Am driving is the present progressive form, describing an action in progress right now.

quests.sentence: We already told the kids about the trip, and they're thrilled.
quests.hint: Focus on 'told' — the announcement itself was a completed past action.
quests.explanation: Told is the simple past form, describing a completed action that led to the kids' current excitement.

quests.sentence: By the time you get this message, I'll probably have landed already.
quests.hint: Reading the message is the future reference point, and landing happens before it.
quests.explanation: Will have landed is the future perfect form, describing an action expected to be complete before a future event.
